svg.title: sky jobs launch: optimization sequence diagram
svg.text: look up storage clouds once per request
With no storage cloud enabled the cached list is empty, so
both lookups in jobs.launch ran the storage check: 4.8 s, then
The second lookup reuses the first answer (0.001 s), keyed by
workspace + config; cleared when the request ends.
≈0.2 s; within phase A noise (6.4–7.2 s).
the first lookup still costs 4.8 s
Request caches are cleared after every request, so each jobs.launch
re-runs the storage check: 4.8 of phase A's 6.8 s.
Cache "no storage cloud" across requests, with a TTL.
ray stop only if Ray runs
ray stop only if Ray runs
Each pod downloaded setuptools<70 from PyPI before ray start:
the pod only checks them (≈2 ms).
Applies once the rebuilt image is published.
pip install skypilot[kubernetes,remote] from PyPI ran before
ray start, and its copy was thrown away later.
ray start runs in the background first; a uv --dry-run warms
the cache meanwhile; wait keeps Ray failures fatal.
ray stop before every ray start: 1.4–3.8 s on a fresh pod with
RAY_STOP_IF_RUNNING: stop only if pgrep finds GCS, raylet or
Head start → whole cluster in Ray 12.95 → 11.37 s.
one blocking Ray wait; skylet meanwhile
Polled once a second; each probe was a kubectl exec that
started 3 Pythons (2.3–4 s). Skylet started only after Ray was
One exec runs a stdlib + GcsClient loop on the head and
returns when all nodes are ALIVE (SKY_RAY_WAIT_DONE).
_run_alongside starts skylet in a thread during the wait.
Runtime setup end → launched 12.5 → 9.4 s (with ej-prj-0).
status + submitted-at in one head command
Two kubectl execs, ≈1.6 s each: status, then submitted-at. The
One codegen prints both payloads; parsed in order. The
executor keeps the status it saw
Saves 1.2–1.7 s; falls back on gRPC or old runtimes.
skip the first-check sleep for finished jobs
Monitor loop slept uniform(0, 15) s before its first check,
though the launch had already seen the job finish.
Terminal status seen at launch → check at once. A job still
RUNNING → SUCCEEDED: random 3.7–16.1 s → steady 3.4–3.6 s.
The steady 3.5 s is the status check plus the end-time fetch.
Reuse the terminal status seen at launch and fetch the end
re-check status when the controller logs
Status re-checked only every 15 s; the ≈3.4 s RUNNING window
was usually missed, so the end was noticed up to 15 s late.
Totals split 46 s / 57 s on a sub-second race.
Re-check as soon as the controller writes its own line (≈15
per launch). The 15 s check stays as a fallback.
Exit 1.3–2.9 s after SUCCEEDED in 8/8 runs (master 1.4–6.7 s).
Client total (sky jobs launch, 8 interleaved runs each)
Remaining: submit 6.8 s (4.8 s storage check) · hand-off 5.6 s · provision 22.5 s · job 7.7 s · checks 7.4 s
